citation: Lopez-Lira, Tang and Zhu (2025), The Memorization Problem: Can We Trust LLMs' Economic Forecasts?, arXiv 2504.14765 v2
text_source: Closed-book recall targets 1990 to 2025: macro series, index levels, WSJ headlines, CRSP month-end prices; masked Capital IQ earnings call transcripts 2006 to 2023 and RavenPack headlines
feature: Recall error for a value on a date; re-identification of firm, year and quarter from entity-neutered text
method: Direct elicitation with GPT-4o (training data to October 2023) and Llama-3.1-70B; before versus after cutoff; fake-cutoff prompts; reconstruction tests; non-identification propositions
outcome: Recall MAPE, directional and threshold accuracy, identification accuracy
incremental_to: Post-cutoff window as control: S&P 500 MAPE 0.61% before and 16.87% after; masked transcripts re-identified 65.77% (large), 40.78% (mid), 30.90% (small caps)
pit_handling: Subject of the paper: evaluate only after the cutoff; prompts and masking fail; memorisation tests are lower bounds; small post-cutoff samples lack power
informs_decision: Splits; no masking; contamination labels (future-invariance); memorisation probe template

citation: Gao, Jiang and Yan (2025), Detecting Lookahead Bias in LLM Forecasts, arXiv 2512.23847 v2 (v1 titled A Test of Lookahead Bias in LLM Forecasts)
text_source: Bloomberg headlines 2012 to 2024 (91,357 in-sample headline-days); StreetEvents earnings call transcripts 2006Q1 to 2024Q1 (106,994 in-sample firm-quarters)
feature: Lookahead Propensity: P(up) + P(down) from a firm-and-date-only recall query with an unknown option
method: Regress outcome on LLM forecast, LAP and their interaction; positive interaction indicates contamination; validation regression; post-cutoff placebo; Llama-3.3-70B (cutoff December 2023)
outcome: Next-day stock return; capex over assets
incremental_to: Interaction 0.162 (t = 3.64) for returns and 0.512 (t = 2.01) for capex, with firm and time fixed effects; insignificant after the cutoff (t = 1.06, 1.35)
pit_handling: Subject of the paper: mean LAP 0.88 in 2020, 0.016 in 2023, about 0 in 2024; needs answer-token probabilities, or repeated sampling where an API hides them
informs_decision: Memorisation probe design; splits; formal test available

citation: Wu, Yang, Ying and Zhou (2025), Anonymization and Information Loss, arXiv 2511.15364 v2
text_source: Seeking Alpha earnings call transcripts, Russell 3000 ETF constituents, November 2022 to December 2024; Yahoo Finance headlines via Finnhub
feature: LLM downgrade-probability and sentiment scores from raw, NER-masked and LLM-rewritten text; anonymisation gap
method: Standalone and horse-race regressions with industry-by-quarter fixed effects and firm controls; score times pre-cutoff interaction; GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, o3-mini (cutoff October 2023)
outcome: S&P rating downgrade; also announcement returns, volatility, capex, sales growth
incremental_to: Raw 6.1 points per SD (t = 5.52) against 4.7 and 4.9 anonymised; in a horse race raw 0.073 (t = 3.58), anonymised -0.012 and -0.007; controls include Z-score and O-score
pit_handling: Main sample postdates the models' cutoff; pre-cutoff interaction insignificant; firm name re-identified 66.88% after NER masking, 9.04% after LLM rewriting, industry 44.01%
informs_decision: No masking (information loss; numbers and agent names carry most signal); splits

citation: He, Lv, Manela and Wu (2025), Chronologically Consistent Large Language Models, arXiv 2502.21206 v3; listed as forthcoming in the Journal of Financial Economics on the author's page
text_source: Dow Jones Newswire firm news, January 2007 to July 2023; pretraining on timestamped open text, 7B tokens before 2000 plus 65B tokens for 2000 to 2024
feature: Embeddings from point-in-time models: ChronoBERT (149M, 1,024-token context) and ChronoGPT (1,552M, 1,792-token context), 26 annual vintages 1999 to 2024
method: Monthly cross-sectional ridge on embeddings; daily decile long-short portfolio; real-time rule uses the previous year's vintage; Ledoit-Wolf Sharpe tests
outcome: Next-day stock return; long-short Sharpe ratio
incremental_to: Sharpe 4.92 (ChronoGPT) and 4.80 (ChronoBERT) against 4.90 for Llama 3.1 8B (p = 0.547, 0.315), 4.18 BERT, 3.86 FinBERT, 3.42 StoriesLM
pit_handling: Each vintage trained only on text dated up to its year; president and event prompts find no post-cutoff knowledge; authors call look-ahead bias modest in this application; Llama's own cutoff is after the test period
informs_decision: Point-in-time reference models exist (MIT licence, huggingface.co/manelalab); candidate leak-free encoder baseline

citation: Glasserman and Lin (2023), Assessing Look-Ahead Bias in Stock Return Predictions Generated By GPT Sentiment Analysis, arXiv 2309.17322 v1
text_source: Financial news headlines, January 2015 to December 2022
feature: GPT-3.5 sentiment from original headlines and from headlines with company identifiers removed
method: Sentiment trading strategies compared inside the training window (to September 2021) and after it (October 2021 to December 2022)
incremental_to: Anonymised headlines outperform originals in sample, more so for larger companies
pit_handling: Separates look-ahead bias from a distraction effect of company knowledge; finds distraction the larger in sample; look-ahead not a concern out of sample
informs_decision: No masking (masking changes the signal for reasons other than look-ahead); splits

citation: Sarkar and Vafa (2024), Lookahead Bias in Pretrained Language Models, working paper dated 28 June 2024 (SSRN 4754678); ICML 2025 DataWorld workshop poster
text_source: Earnings calls, September to November 2019 and 2018 (1,000 calls); candidate biographies for close US House elections
feature: Risk factors generated for the following year; predicted election winner; re-identified firm and year
method: One-sided tests resting on events assumed unpredictable; Llama-2 70B (cutoff July 2023); censoring tests with GPT-4
outcome: Leakage frequency; accuracy on close elections; re-identification rate
incremental_to: COVID-19 named in 6.8% of risk forecasts made from 2019 calls; close-election winners predicted with 70% to 80% accuracy
pit_handling: An instruction not to use future information fails; GPT-4 names the firm in 70% of calls with the name censored and 61% with name and products censored; inferred year correlates 0.79 with the true year
informs_decision: No masking; formal test available; report pre- and post-cutoff results separately

citation: Engelberg, Manela, Mullins and Vulicevic (2025), Entity Neutering, working paper (SSRN 5182756; SSRN page returned HTTP 403, abstract read on a co-author's page)
text_source: Financial news articles (over 500,000 per the abstract); also MD&As and earnings call transcripts
feature: Sentiment from raw and from entity-neutered text
method: An LLM masks and paraphrases repeatedly until a separate LLM cannot name the firm; compares sentiment and return predictability
outcome: Firm re-identification; sentiment agreement; return predictability
incremental_to: Among unidentified articles raw and neutered sentiment agree more than 90% of the time with similar return predictability
pit_handling: Neutering offered as the remedy; LLMs identify the firm at the rate of random chance after neutering; raw minus neutered gap as an upper bound on look-ahead bias
informs_decision: No masking (the main evidence against the default; conflicts with transcript results in Lopez-Lira et al.)

citation: Ludwig, Mullainathan and Rambachan (2025), Large Language Models: An Applied Econometric Framework, NBER Working Paper 33344, arXiv 2412.07031 v4
feature: LLM outputs used as predictors or as measurements
method: Econometric conditions: prediction requires no training leakage between the LLM's training data and the researcher's sample; estimation requires a validation sample
pit_handling: States the no-training-leakage condition; to be met by model choice and research design
informs_decision: Splits; contamination labels; main home is the statistical-method stream (validation sample for LLM labels)

citation: Roy and Roy (2026), MemGuard-Alpha: Limits of Membership Inference for Detecting and Filtering Memorization-Contaminated Signals in LLM-Based Financial Forecasting, arXiv 2603.26797 v2
text_source: LLM-generated trading signals (details not in the abstract)
feature: Membership-inference scores as a memorisation detector
method: Tests whether the scores separate memorised from clean signals and whether filtering on them improves returns
outcome: Detection discrimination; risk-adjusted returns after costs
incremental_to: A date feature reproduces the cutoff-defined label; dropping the weakest model beats every filter
pit_handling: After within-model normalisation the scores discriminate near chance; no contamination filter improves returns after costs
informs_decision: Memorisation probe (do not use membership-inference scores)

citation: Sarkar (2024), StoriesLM: A Family of Language Models With Time-Indexed Training Data, SSRN 4881024 (paper page returned HTTP 403; this row comes from the Hugging Face cards and the author's project page, not the paper)
text_source: v2 corpus 1750 to 2024: American Stories newspapers, public-domain books, an arXiv subset, Congressional Record, newswire
feature: Point-in-time encoders: 125 annual vintages 1900 to 2024, ModernBERT-base, about 0.1B parameters, 512-token sequences
method: Sequential continued pretraining, one year at a time
pit_handling: Each model sees only text up to its vintage year; author notes thin data for 1960 to 2020; no licence on the model card

citation: Drinkall, Rahimikia, Pierrehumbert and Zohren (2024), Time Machine GPT, Findings of NAACL 2024, arXiv 2404.18543
text_source: WMT News Crawl and Wikipedia (model card)
feature: Point-in-time GPT-2-class generative models, one per cutoff year
method: Train a separate model on text up to each cutoff
pit_handling: Designed to hold no knowledge of later facts or language change; 12 repos under huggingface.co/Ti-Ma (2013 to 2022 seen), CC0-1.0 on the 2022 card

citation: He, Lv, Manela and Wu (2025), Instruction Tuning Chronologically Consistent Language Models, arXiv 2510.11677 v2
text_source: Dow Jones Newswire headlines, January 2007 to July 2023
feature: Headline labelled favourable, unfavourable or unclear by a point-in-time instruction-tuned model (about 1.55B parameters, 1,792-token context, vintages 1999 to 2024)
method: Instruction tuning on over 425,000 pairs screened by GPT-4.1 for pre-2000 knowledge; long-short portfolio on the label
outcome: Next-day stock return; long-short Sharpe ratio
incremental_to: Sharpe 0.95 against 1.53 (Qwen-1.5-1.8B-Chat) and 1.76 (Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct); authors read this as at least 54% to 62% of predictability surviving without leakage
pit_handling: Point-in-time weights and tuning data; president and event prompts find no post-cutoff knowledge; win rate against Qwen-1.5-1.8B-Chat is 12.59% to 16.79%
informs_decision: Point-in-time generative models exist but follow instructions poorly (MIT licence)

citation: Yan, Tang, Gao, Jiang and Lu (2026), DatedGPT: Preventing Lookahead Bias in Large Language Models with Time-Aware Pretraining, arXiv 2603.11838 v2
feature: Twelve 1.3B-parameter point-in-time models with annual cutoffs 2013 to 2024, about 100B training tokens each, plus per-year instruction data
method: Train from scratch per cutoff; perplexity probing of the knowledge boundary; return prediction with models whose training does or does not cover the outcome period
incremental_to: Models whose training covers the outcome period add 26.4 basis points per standard deviation (1% level); Sharpe 3.20 in the bias-free setup
pit_handling: Strict annual cutoffs; perplexity probing bounds each model's knowledge at its cutoff year; base and instruct weights at huggingface.co/datedgpt (standard Llama architecture, 2,048-token context, no licence on the card)
informs_decision: Point-in-time generative models exist; size of look-ahead bias in news-return tests
